[DECISION] REJECT

[FEEDBACK] FND cannot be diagnosed without documented positive physical exam findings inconsistent with organic disease *and* exclusion of structural, vascular, metabolic, and inflammatory etiologies. Required before considering FND: (1) completed and reported right arm musculoskeletal/neurovascular exam (including pulse, capillary refill, sensation, strength, range of motion, Spurling’s, Adson’s, Roos’ tests); (2) review of all pending studies — especially right arm radiographs (to rule out occult fracture), ECG (to assess for atrial fibrillation or ischemia), serum CK (rhabdomyolysis), and BMP (electrolytes, calcium, creatinine); (3) documentation of at least one positive functional sign (e.g., tremor entrainment, give-way weakness, or non-dermatomal sensory pattern). Without these, FND is unjustified.
